blocks.raw: <Tip>Node = where you GO TO and PASS THROUGH (junction, hub). Landmark = what you LOOK AT for direction (not entered). This is the highest-frequency error: students confuse nodes and landmarks. Test yourself: "Does the object primarily function as a gathering/transfer point (node) or as a visual reference (landmark)?"</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing nodes and landmarks — remember: Node = place you go TO; Landmark = thing you look AT. A church can be both, but you must identify its PRIMARY function in context.","Thinking edges must be water bodies — edges can be any linear boundary: walls, highways, railroad cuts, development edges, even ridgelines. The key is that they separate and are NOT used as movement channels.","Assuming all major streets are paths — paths are channels through which you move. A walled-off highway embankment, even if major, is more edge than path if you cannot move along it.","Using 'landmark' to mean 'important site' — in Lynch's framework, landmarks are specifically things you look AT for orientation, not things you visit."]} />
